lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Lord and King! Our Zeus below! And you, daughter of Demeter! Do not ignore a lover's petition.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What exactly do you want from us? And who are you?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I am Protesilaus, son of Iphiclus, from Phylace. A soldier of the Greeks, and the first man to die at Troy. I am asking for a brief leave of absence to return to life.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Every dead man wants that, Protesilaus. Not one of them gets it.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: But I don't love life, Hades. I love my wife. She was a new bride. I left her in our bedroom and sailed away, and then—unlucky as I am—Hector killed me the moment I stepped off the ship. My love for her is tearing me apart, Lord. I just want to go up, see her even for a little while, and come straight back down.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Didn't you drink from the Lethe, Protesilaus?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I did, Lord. But the feeling was stronger than the water.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Then just wait. She'll show up here eventually, and you won't need to go up at all.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I cannot bear the delay, Pluto. You've been in love yourself. You know what it's like.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: And what good will it do you to live for one day, only to come back down a moment later and start crying all over again?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I think I can persuade her to come back down with me. Instead of one dead soul, you'll get two.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: It is against regulations. It has never been done.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Let me remind you, Pluto: you handed Eurydice over to Orpheus for exactly this reason. And you sent my kinswoman Alcestis back up as a personal favour to Heracles.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: [Sighs] And do you really want to appear to your beautiful bride as a bare, hideous skull? How is she supposed to embrace you when she can't even recognise you? I promise you, she will be terrified, she will run away, and you will have made the long trip up for nothing.

lines.speaker: Persephone
lines.text: Then fix that too, husband. Tell Hermes that the moment Protesilaus reaches the sunlight, he should tap him with his wand and turn him back into the handsome young man he was when he left the bridal chamber.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: [Pause] If Persephone approves. Hermes, take him up and make him a bridegroom again. [To Protesilaus] And you. Remember: you get one day.
